the ell of Venice. At Goa, and other parts, they
they ufe a larger cando, equal to feventeen Dutch
ells; exceeding that of Babel and Balfora by *per*
_centum_, and the vera by 64. In Siam, they ufe the
ken, short of three Paris feet by one inch. The ken
contains two folks, the fok two keubs, the keub twelve
nious or inches, the niou to be equal to eight grains of
rice, i. e. to about nine lines. At Camboia, they ufe
the hafler ; in Japan, the tatam ; and the fpan on fome
of the coafts of Guinea.<x_0.999><y_0.9992><class_Text>
